The Quarry Road Journal

Notes on stonework, weather and the long way round

Limestone in March

Posted on 3 March 2026 by the editor

The quarry reopened this week after the frost, and the first cut came out cleaner than anyone expected. We walked the top road at dawn and counted eleven herons on the flooded floor of the lower pit, which is eleven more than last spring.

Work resumes on the north face on Monday, weather allowing. The stonemasons' co-operative has asked for another fortnight before the first delivery, and given the state of the access track that seems entirely reasonable.

On mortar, again

Posted on 18 February 2026 by the editor

Every year somebody writes in to say that lime mortar is a fashion, and every year the same wall falls down to prove otherwise. We are not going to relitigate this, but here are the photographs.

The short version: match the mortar to the stone, not to the century you wish the building had been put up in.

The winter list

Posted on 9 January 2026 by the editor

Gates, gutters, the pump house roof, and the long-promised index of back issues. In roughly that order, and probably not before April.
